533a47bbc00e938e.title: Tinlicker North America 2026
533a47bbc00e938e.desc: Over more than a decade, Tinlicker have consistently pushed boundaries in the world of electronic music, cultivating a sound that is both unique and personal. The use of real instruments, ranging from strings to keys to horns, has long been a staple of the ensemble that helps to separate their sound from more traditional dance acts. Beyond the instrumentation, their music also has an unusual and powerful propensity to evoke an array of feelings, from euphoria to sadness, and everything in between. It’s music one can dance to, no doubt, but it’s also music that tells a compelling story. After their 2021 breakthrough with single ‘Because You Move Me’ (over 1 billion streams now), Tinlicker implemented some radical changes - they left their long-time label, Anjunadeep for [PIAS] and transitioned from performing purely DJ sets to a format including live/band performances. Risky but well-calculated choices, necessary for the next steps to realize the creative direction of the album they were working on, ‘Cold Enough For Snow’ (2024). The resulting LP was a masterclass in balancing innovation with quality. Reroute to remain. Stylistically diverse, it includes melodic (‘Glasshouse’) to…

531d4399eeedd715.title: Maddie Zahm: Everything All The Time Tour
531d4399eeedd715.desc: Maddie Zahm is sad & sexy-forever oscillating through the spectrum of emotions and inviting fans into the reality that existing is overwhelming. Maddie embraces a kind of unapologetic yet compassionate truth-telling in her lyrics where she inevitably leads listeners into the most intimate parts of her psyche (and theirs too). The virality of singles, “Fat Funny Friend” & “You Might Not Like Her,” have translated into over 175 million streams and millions of fans turned tight knit community on TikTok. After the release of her 2023 debut album “Now That I’ve Been Honest” and 2024 fan favorite “little me”, Maddie is emerging from almost a year of introspection after launching into the spotlight just a few years ago. Her upcoming project shows the side of her process that she likes the idea of compartmentalizing but wants to share with all who have navigated their own stages of grief. Her headline tour begins in Houston on 3/21/25 with first single “Sheets” kicking off her next era of music.

53ed4384d7559a22.title: Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal with Rafael Payare
53ed4384d7559a22.desc: Orchestre Symphonique de Montréal and its brilliant music director Rafael Payare step onto the Walt Disney Concert Hall stage with Shostakovich’s powerful, energetic, and darkly intense Tenth Symphony. Following a performance of Shostakovich’s 10th on Montréal’s 2022 tour, Bachtrack wrote that “Payare’s twitchy baton...dug into the work’s spirit of grim survival against adversity. It was composed in the wake of Stalin’s death, the ferocious second movement often described as a musical portrait of the dictator. Payare took it at a lightning lick, a bundle of energy on the podium.” Samy Moussa’s otherworldly and mythological Elysium opens the program, followed by one of the most treasured violin concertos of all time performed by Greek violinist Leonidas Kavakos—whose “talent dazzles from the first notes” (Bachtrack). This performance is generously supported by the Colburn Foundation.

535998194440454b.title: Elf The Musical
535998194440454b.desc: Elf, the hit Hollywood blockbuster movie has been supersized into a live theatre spectacular for this Christmas. With a massive stage featuring amazing film backdrops on a huge led screen, plus a cast that travels through the auditorium, everyone gets a close-up view of the action. The presentation features Santa’s flying sleigh, an audience snowball fight, indoor snowstorm, a giant candy cane journey from the North Pole, aerial cirque stars and giant tv screens so you don’t miss any of the spectacle. The story is hilariously recreated by a large cast of performers into the biggest live Christmas show in the UK. This Christmas Spectacular production features a book written by Bob Martin and Thomas Meehan (Annie, The Producers and Hairspray) and an original score of great songs by Matt Sklar and Chad Beguel in that has delighted audiences on Broadway and the West End.
